messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A quiet corner of the workshop between jobs; then one label is peeling even though you remember what it means. There is enough time to fuss with it if you want. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "I scrape the peeling label from the drawer and put it back. I rub the old groove once, then try the next job. If the corner still catches, I leave it alone and mark the next one."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "I press the peel with my thumbnail. The crack shows where the paper caught. I leave the corner alone and turn the clock once."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "1. stop. 2. check the watch. slow. 3. peel the label. 4. check the dust. 5. check the tinkered watch. 6. check the tinkered piece. 7. i keep it tidy. 8. ask the watch for the date. 9. check the corner. 10. i mark it."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i touch the peel once with my thumbnail, then stop. the label stays on the corner. i put the peel on the bench and leave the corner where it fell. the work goes. i keep the label beside the bench."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I rub the peeling label with my thumb. “keep.” i move the label closer. i put it in my pocket and leave it there. i take the rusted bolt from the corner and test its edge. if it works, i leave the bolt there too."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i press the label against the corner, then tap the page edge twice. “one,” i say, and write “two” beside it. i leave the peeling corner aside and tap the page edge twice with my fingertip, then write “three” next to the label."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i tap the label. i peel it. i leave the job."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i keep the label beside the corner and tap the peeling edge with my knuckle. if it stays, i mark the spot with a pencil line instead of peeling it."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i mark the peeling label with a pencil first, then turn it by hand. i leave the corner alone for one minute, then leave it alone again. if the label still peels, i leave the corner alone for one more minute, then mark it again."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "I stop the seed tin beside the peeling label. The peeling starts. I put the tin back, then the seed tin. I look at the label. \"Not here.\" I put the tin back. \"The seed stays.\" I wait for the peeling to stop."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i peel the label back, then put it back on the wall. the peeling makes a small line. i put the label back on the wall again. the corner stays open. i move the wall so the line disappears."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "I scrape the peeling edge once with my thumbnail. \"I mark it,\" I say. I put the label down, scrape once more, and look at the cracked edge. Then I say, \"I mark it again. I mark it once more. I mark it again.\" I scrape the edge once more, then mark it again."}]
